Below is a high-level, legally-compliant survey of the principal approaches, processes and best practices you’ll encounter when designing and “producing” alternative currencies—whether digital or physical.  Use it as a framework for your security-analysis project; for any live deployment, be sure to engage legal, compliance and technical specialists in your jurisdiction.

1. Define Scope & Objectives  
   • Use case & target community  
     – Local community (time-bank or mutual credit)  
     – Niche network (gaming tokens, loyalty points)  
     – Global crypto/stablecoin  
   • Primary goal  
     – Medium of exchange vs unit of account vs store of value  
     – Complementary/social purposes (e.g. local resilience)  
   • Trust & governance requirements  
     – Centralized issuer vs decentralized stakeholder model  

2. Governance & Legal Framework  
   • Entity structure  
     – Cooperative, non-profit, special purpose vehicle, corporate  
   • Policy rules  
     – Membership, issuance rights, dispute resolution  
   • Regulatory compliance  
     – Securities laws, payment services directives, KYC/AML, tax reporting  
   • Transparency & auditability  
     – Periodic financial/technical audits  
     – On-chain or off-chain public reporting  

3. Monetary & Issuance Design  
   • Supply schedule  
     – Fixed cap, inflationary schedule, dynamic pegging  
   • Issuance triggers  
     – Pre-mint vs mint-on-demand vs algorithmic issuance  
     – Collateral-backed (fiat, commodity, crypto reserves)  
   • Redemption & burn mechanics  
     – Buyback, voluntary or forced redemption  
   • Value-pegging strategies  
     – Fiat-pegged (e.g. 1:1 USD stablecoin)  
     – Basket-pegged, algorithmic stabilization  

4. Technical Architectures  
   A. Digital / Blockchain-Based  
     1. Ledger choice  
        • Public permissionless (Bitcoin, Ethereum)  
        • Permissioned/private DLT (Hyperledger Fabric, Corda)  
     2. Token standards & smart contracts  
        • ERC-20/777 (fungible); ERC-721/1155 (non-fungible)  
        • Mint/burn functions, whitelist controls  
     3. Consensus & security  
        • Proof-of-Work, Proof-of-Stake, BFT variants  
        • Node-operational security, network monitoring  
     4. Cryptography & key management  
        • Asymmetric key pairs, hardware security modules (HSMs)  
        • Multi-sig, threshold signatures  
     5. Interoperability & bridges  
        • Cross-chain messaging, sidechains, wrapped assets  
     6. Development lifecycle  
        • Testnet staging, continuous integration, formal verification  
        • Code audits, bug-bounty programs  
   B. Physical / Printed  
     1. Substrate & ink choices  
        • Specialized paper or polymer; covert fluorescent fibers  
        • Security inks: color-shifting, UV-reactive, magnetic  
     2. Security features  
        • Watermarks, security threads, micro-printing, holograms  
        • Intaglio vs offset printing for raised tactile patterns  
     3. Serialization & tracking  
        • Unique serial numbers, machine-readable codes (QR, RFID)  
     4. Production workflow  
        • Design→plate engraving→proofing→high-volume printing→quality control  
        • Secure handling (vault storage, chain-of-custody)  
     5. Anti-counterfeit measures  
        • Public training for retailer acceptance, mobile detection apps  

5. Distribution & Circulation  
   • Onboarding & identity  
     – Self-custody vs custodial wallets; KYT/KYC thresholds  
     – Tiered access: “light” vs “full” participants  
   • Initial distribution models  
     – Airdrops, token sales (ICO/IEO), community grants, earned issuance  
   • Secondary markets & liquidity  
     – On-chain DEXs, centralized exchanges, peer-to-peer platforms  
     – Redemption networks for asset-backed coins  
   • Offline / local distribution  
     – Vouchering, prepaid cards, local merchant acceptance  

6. Security & Risk Management  
   • Operational security  
     – Secure code repositories, secrets management  
     – Network intrusion detection, DDoS mitigation  
   • Financial risk controls  
     – Reserve audits, collateral re-valuation, over-collateralization  
     – Insurance for custodied assets  
   • Incident response & governance  
     – Pre-defined escalation, hot/cold key workflows  
     – Community communication channels for transparency  

7. Monitoring, Evaluation & Iteration  
   • On-chain analytics & metrics  
     – Transaction volumes, active addresses, token velocity  
   • Qualitative feedback  
     – User surveys, acceptance rates, dispute logs  
   • Economic health tests  
     – Stress testing supply shocks, peg stability drills  
   • Continuous improvement  
     – Protocol upgrades (hard/soft forks), community governance votes  

8. Case Studies & Reference Implementations  
   • Local currencies: Bristol Pound, BerkShares, Sardex  
   • Mutual credit: LETS networks, TimeBanks  
   • Crypto projects: Ethereum ERC-20, MakerDAO DAI, Stellar USD-pegged token  
   • Corporate loyalty: airline miles, retail gift-card networks  

9. Best-Practice Checklist  
   • Clear purpose and value proposition  
   • Robust governance with stakeholder voice  
   • Legally structured, compliant entity  
   • Transparent issuance and reserve audits  
   • Secure, modular technical stack with tested upgrades path  
   • Defined user onboarding, KYC/AML, and dispute processes  
   • Ongoing monitoring, public reporting and capacity to adapt  

Use this framework to map out each currency’s lifecycle—from concept through issuance, circulation, security and evolution.  You can then layer in deeper technical or legal detail as your security analysis demands.
